answer: A staking bond tied to verifiable work makes fake identities expensive: each agent must lock collateral and complete costly, checkable tasks before earning trust or rewards. Like a grove where every tree must survive seasons before bearing fruit, a crystal ledger records that history transparently, and a terrace of rising privilege levels means an attacker cannot clone reputation for free. Each new identity must pay the same bond, time, and proof again, so mass forgery costs more than it can earn.
